findings.passage: This requires the secretary of state and the coordinator of elections to create a portal that would check as to whether or not someone is a convicted felon or if they are a U.S. citizen prior to them being actually registered to vote,
findings.note: Committee remarks on HB 69, quoted by The Tennessee Conservative (article dated 2025-03-20, committee meeting the Wednesday before).

findings.passage: When somebody goes down to register to vote right now, there’s nothing that checks that.
findings.note: Committee remarks on HB 69 as quoted by The Tennessee Conservative; says current registration has no citizenship check.

findings.passage: It would ensure that only U.S. citizens and only those that have not been convicted of felonies or had their rights restored after having been convicted of a felony, would be actually voting.
findings.note: Committee remarks on HB 69 as quoted by The Tennessee Conservative.

findings.passage: When one person votes illegally, it cancels out a legal citizen’s solemn right to decide who will lead in our communities, our state, and our nation,
findings.note: Statement issued in his name in the House caucus press release announcing HB 69, as quoted by The Tennessee Conservative.

findings.passage: Non-US citizens and convicted felons who have not had their rights restored should not be able to vote. Today, @SenJohnson [Sen. Jack Johnson] @Jodyforstaterep [Rep. Jody Barrett] & I filed HB 69, strengthening accountability in our electoral process and reaffirming our duty to Tennesseans to ensure integrity at the ballot box,
findings.note: His post on X about filing HB 69, as quoted by The Tennessee Conservative (bracketed names are the outlet's).
